## Contents of this Practice Direction

## 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –] Section I – Provisions about patents and those other rights within the scope of Section I of Part 63

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –] Section II – Provisions about registered trade marks and other intellectual property rights

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –] Section III – Provisions about appeals

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –] Section IV – Provisions about final orders

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 1.1 This practice direction is divided into five sections –] Section V – Provisions about proceedings in the Intellectual Property Enterprise Court

## Scope of Section I

## 2.1 This Section applies to claims within the scope of Section 1 of Part 63. ## Starting the claim (rule 63.5)

## 3.1 A claim form to which this Section applies must–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 3.1 A claim form to which this Section applies must–] (a) be marked ‘Chancery Division Patents Court’ or ‘Chancery Division Intellectual Property Enterprise Court’ as the case may be, in the top right hand corner below the title of the court, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 3.1 A claim form to which this Section applies must–] (b) state the number of any patent or registered design to which the claim relates. ## Claim for infringement or challenge to validity (rule 63.6)

## 4.1 In a claim for infringement of a patent –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.1 In a claim for infringement of a patent –] (1) the statement of case must–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.1 In a claim for infringement of a patent –] (a) show which of the claims in the specification of the patent are alleged to be infringed; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.1 In a claim for infringement of a patent –] (b) give at least one example of each type of infringement alleged; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.1 In a claim for infringement of a patent –] (2) a copy of each document referred to in the statement of case, and where necessary a translation of the document, must be served with the statement of case. ## 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (1) the statement of case must contain particulars of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (a) the remedy sought; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (b) the issues except those relating to validity of the patent or registered design;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (2) the statement of case must have a separate document attached to and forming part of it headed ‘Grounds of Invalidity’ which must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (a) specify the grounds on which validity of the patent or registered design is challenged; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (b) include particulars that will clearly define every issue (including any challenge to any claimed priority date) which it is intended to raise; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (3) a copy of each document referred to in the Grounds of Invalidity, and where necessary a translation of the document, must be served with the Grounds of Invalidity. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] 4.3 Where in an application in which the validity of a patent or a registered design is challenged, the Grounds of Invalidity include an allegation –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (1) that the invention is not a patentable invention because it is not new or does not include an inventive step, the particulars must specify details of the matter in the state of the art relied on, as set out in paragraph 4.4;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (2) that the specification of the patent does not disclose the invention clearly enough and completely enough for it to be performed by a person skilled in the art, the particulars must state, if appropriate, which examples of the invention cannot be made to work and in which respects they do not work or do not work as described in the specification; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.2 Where the validity of a patent or registered design is challenged –] (3) that the registered design is not new or lacks individual character, the particulars must specify details of any prior design relied on, as set out in paragraph 4.4. ## 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (1) in the case of matter or a design made available to the public by written description, the date on which and the means by which it was so made available, unless this is clear from the fact of the matter; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (2) in the case of matter or a design made available to the public by use –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (a) the date or dates of such use;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (b) the name of all persons making such use;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (c) the place of such use;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (d) any written material which identifies such use;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (e) the existence and location of any apparatus employed in such use; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] (f) all facts and matters relied on to establish that such matter was made available to the public. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] 4.5 In any proceedings in which the validity of a patent is challenged, where a party alleges that machinery or apparatus was used before the priority date of the claim the court may order inspection of that machinery or apparatus. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 4.4 The details required under paragraphs 4.3(1) and 4.3(3) are –] 4.6 If the validity of a patent is challenged on the ground that the invention did not involve an inventive step, a party who wishes to rely on the commercial success of the patent must state in the statement of case the grounds on which that party so relies. ## Case management (rule 63.8)

## 5.1 The following paragraphs only of Practice Direction 29 apply –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.1 The following paragraphs only of Practice Direction 29 apply –] (1) paragraph 5 (case management conferences)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.1 The following paragraphs only of Practice Direction 29 apply –] (a) excluding paragraph 5.9; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.1 The following paragraphs only of Practice Direction 29 apply –] (b) modified so far as is made necessary by other specific provisions of this practice direction; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.1 The following paragraphs only of Practice Direction 29 apply –] (2) paragraph 7 (failure to comply with case management directions). ## 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (1) a judge of the Patents Court, or a Master, but

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (2) a Master may only deal with the following matters –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (a) orders by way of settlement, except settlement of procedural disputes;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (b) applications for extension of time;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (c) applications for permission to serve out of the jurisdiction;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (d) applications for security for costs;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (e) other matters as directed by a judge of the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] (f) enforcement of money judgments. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] 5.3 The claimant must apply for a case management conference within 14 days of the date when all defendants who intend to file and serve a defence have done so. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] 5.4 Where the claim has been transferred, the claimant must apply for a case management conference within 14 days of the date of the order transferring the claim, unless the court held or gave directions for a case management conference when it made the order transferring the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] 5.5 Any party may, at a time earlier than that provided in paragraphs 5.3 and 5.4, apply in writing to the court to fix a case management conference. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.2 Case management of proceedings in the Patents Court will be dealt with by –] 5.6 If the claimant does not make an application in accordance with paragraphs 5.3 and 5.4, any other party may apply for a case management conference. ## 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] 5.8 Not less than 4 days before a case management conference, each party must file and serve an application notice for any order which that party intends to seek at the case management conference. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] 5.9 Unless the court orders otherwise, the claimant, or the party who makes an application under paragraph 5.6, in consultation with the other parties, must prepare a case management bundle containing –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] (1) the claim form;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] (2) all other statements of case (excluding schedules), except that, if a summary of a statement of case has been filed, the bundle must contain the summary, and not the full statement of case;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] (3) a pre-trial timetable, if one has been agreed or ordered;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] (4) the principal orders of the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] (5) any agreement in writing made by the parties as to disclosure,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.7 The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative.] and provide copies of the case management bundle for the court and the other parties at least 4 days before the first case management conference or any earlier hearing at which the court may give case management directions. ## 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (1) a scientific adviser under section 70(3) of the Senior Courts Act 1981 or under section 63(1) of the County Courts Act 1984 be appointed; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (2) a document setting out basic undisputed technology should be prepared. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (Rule 35.15 applies to scientific advisers.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] 5.11 Where a trial date has not been fixed by the court, a party may apply for a trial date by filing a certificate which must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (1) state the estimated length of the trial, agreed if possible by all parties;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (2) detail the time required for the judge to consider the documents;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (3) identify the area of technology; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] (4) assess the complexity of the technical issues involved by indicating the complexity on a scale of 1 to 5 (with 1 being the least and 5 the most complex). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 5.10 At the case management conference the court may direct that –] 5.12 The claimant, in consultation with the other parties, must revise and update the documents, referred to in paragraph 5.9 appropriately as the case proceeds. This must include making all necessary revisions and additions at least 7 days before any subsequent hearing at which the court may give case management directions. ## Disclosure and inspection (rule 63.9)

## 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (1) the infringement of a patent by a product or process where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (a) not less than 21 days before the date for service of a list of documents the defendant notifies the claimant and any other party of the defendant’s intention to serve–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (i) full particulars of the product or process alleged to infringe; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (ii) any necessary drawings or other illustrations; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (b) on or before the date for service the defendant serves on the claimant and any other party the documents referred to in paragraph 6.1(1)(a);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (2) any ground on which the validity of a patent is put in issue, except documents which came into existence within the period –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (a) beginning two years before the earliest claimed priority date; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (b) ending two years after that date; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (3) the issue of commercial success. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] 6.2 The particulars served under paragraph 6.1(1)(b) must be accompanied by a signed written statement which must state that the person making the statement –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (1) is personally acquainted with the facts to which the particulars relate;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (2) verifies that the particulars are a true and complete description of the product or process alleged to infringe; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (3) understands that he or she may be required to attend court in order to be cross-examined on the contents of the particulars. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] 6.3 Where the issue of commercial success arises, the patentee must, within such time limit as the court may direct, serve a schedule containing –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (1) where the commercial success relates to an article or product –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (a) an identification of the article or product (for example by product code number) which the patentee asserts has been made in accordance with the claims of the patent;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (b) a summary by convenient periods of sales of any such article or product;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (c) a summary for the equivalent periods of sales, if any, of any equivalent prior article or product marketed before the article or product in sub-paragraph (a); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (d) a summary by convenient periods of any expenditure on advertising and promotion which supported the marketing of the articles or products in sub-paragraphs (a) and (c); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (2) where the commercial success relates to the use of a process –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (a) an identification of the process which the patentee asserts has been used in accordance with the claims of the patent;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (b) a summary by convenient periods of the revenue received from the use of such process;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (c) a summary for the equivalent periods of the revenues, if any, received from the use of any equivalent prior art process; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 6.1 Standard disclosure does not require the disclosure of documents that relate to –] (d) a summary by convenient periods of any expenditure which supported the use of the process in sub-paragraphs (a) and (c). ## Experiments

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Experiments] 7.1 A party seeking to establish any fact by experimental proof conducted for the purpose of litigation must, at least 21 days before service of the application notice for directions under paragraph 7.3, or within such other time as the court may direct, serve on all parties a notice–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Experiments] (1) stating the facts which the party seeks to establish; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Experiments] (2) giving full particulars of the experiments proposed to establish them. ## 7.2 A party served with a notice under paragraph 7.1–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 7.2 A party served with a notice under paragraph 7.1–] (1) must within 21 days after such service, serve on the other party a notice stating whether or not each fact is admitted; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 7.2 A party served with a notice under paragraph 7.1–] (2) may request the opportunity to inspect a repetition of all or a number of the experiments identified in the notice served under paragraph 7.1. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 7.2 A party served with a notice under paragraph 7.1–] 7.3 Where any fact which a party seeks to establish by experimental proof is not admitted, that party must apply to the court for permission and directions by application notice. ## Use of models or apparatus

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Use of models or apparatus] 8.1 A party that intends to rely on any model or apparatus must apply to the court for directions at the first case management conference. ## Time estimates for trial, trial bundle, reading guide and detailed trial timetable

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Time estimates for trial, trial bundle, reading guide and detailed trial timetable] 9.1 Not less than one week before the beginning of the trial, each party must inform the court in writing of the estimated length of its –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Time estimates for trial, trial bundle, reading guide and detailed trial timetable] (1) oral submissions;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Time estimates for trial, trial bundle, reading guide and detailed trial timetable] (2) examination in chief, if any, of its own witnesses; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > Time estimates for trial, trial bundle, reading guide and detailed trial timetable] (3) cross-examination of witnesses of any other party. ## 9.2 At least four days before the date fixed for the trial, the claimant must file –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 63 – INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY CLAIMS > 9.2 At least four days before the date fixed for the trial, the claimant must file –] (1) the trial bundle;
